sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL4411 .W38 2002x
sources.note: Nothing on word stress. Describes 'standard Wa' = Diffloth's Wa proper (Parauk, para1301), explicitly not the Vo group. Ch.4 treats syllable structure, sesquisyllabicity and the /s./ presyllable (4.1.7, 4.2.1, 5.4.1) and register; 6.6 'emphatic tone' mentions utterance-final high/long emphasis. Full-text search for stress/accent/prominence/iambic/unstressed found no word-stress statement.

sources.note: For Meung Yum (a Wa variety of Kunlong Township, Shan State; NOT this glottocode) 3.4 p.54: 'Mon-Khmer languages are monosyllable and iambic, meaning that if the word is not monosyllable, then a light syllable is followed by a stressed heavy syllable. Meung Yum shares this structure'; 3.6: 'Meung Yum has no contrastive stress; stress is predictable. The stress pattern is iambic.' Its ch.6.2.3 (pp.114-116) summarises Zhou, Yan & Chen 2004:22-26 on Meng Gong, the representative point of the Wa/Vax (=Vo, Yongde) dialect, i.e. this language: 31 consonants incl. retroflexes in Chinese loans, 12 cl…

sources.note: Silent on stress. Yaong Soi dialect = Wa Parauk (para1301). 2.2.3 (p.17): syllable = presyllable (C-obstruent + schwa, bound) + main syllable C1(C2)V1(V2)(V3)(C3); no stress/accent statement anywhere (full-text search).
